description: +++===+++ 2026-10-14 — Hasan Alizada — HAAL-014. Central registry of Haalendar atoms. Read this file first; then load only the contract, vectors and implementation of the atoms involved. Update it after every change.

conventions.id_pattern: <domain>.<name>.v<major> — folder atoms/<id>/ holds contract.json, vectors.json, examples.md
conventions.contract_format: JSON with input/output as JSON Schema 2020-12, errors, events, invariants, requirements
conventions.hash_input: UTF-8 bytes of contract.json followed by vectors.json, line endings normalized to LF; stored as b3:<hex>

atoms.purpose: Returns the Week A/B label of a date counted from a user-chosen anchor week; correct across year boundaries and 53-week years.
atoms.notes: Pure function. Never use ISO week number parity. Implemented in HAAL-045 (Python and TypeScript, both pass vectors.json); the Settings preview uses it now, the calendar header in HAAL-085.

atoms.purpose: Occurrence dates of an event inside a window (≤ 367 days): one-off, daily, weekly, monthly (short months skipped), yearly (29 February only in leap years), without exceptions; tells whether an RRULE is supported.
atoms.notes: Pure function on dates; times are applied per occurrence with time.local_to_utc.v1 and viewer days come from time.event_days.v1. The server validates rrule with it (HAAL-066); the day/week/month views expand series with it (HAAL-060, 087, 088). Extended rules (HAAL-092) arrive as v2.

atoms.purpose: Display order of the entries of one day: all-day first, then by start (continuing entries count as 00:00 and come first), then by title ignoring case and accents, then creation time and key; colour never counts.
atoms.notes: Pure function; plain code-point comparisons so both implementations agree. The day view uses it (HAAL-060); agenda and export later.

atoms.purpose: ISO 8601 week number (1..53) and ISO week-based year of a date — the selected date, never today.
atoms.notes: Pure function on dates. The calendar header uses it (HAAL-062); mini month week numbers (HAAL-097), week view and exports later.

atoms.purpose: Checks a new password against the Haalendar password policy (15..128 chars, not common, no e-mail/name, enough variety) and returns every violated rule.
atoms.notes: Common list bundled in backend/src/haalendar/accounts/data/common_passwords.txt (SecLists, MIT); the TypeScript implementation imports the same file. TypeScript gives live hints in forms; the server result is authoritative.

atoms.purpose: Decides whether a user may read, write items of, manage or share a container (calendar, board, note) from ownership and an active share; default deny, admins get no content access; maps refusals to 404 (not readable) or 403.
atoms.notes: Server entry point: haalendar.authz.require (loads owner and share under row-level security). PostgreSQL RLS (haalendar.security.rls) enforces the same rules as a second layer; the isolation suite is backend/tests/test_isolation.py. Sharing API: haalendar.sharing (HAAL-167).

atoms.purpose: Converts a local date and time in an IANA zone into the UTC instant it denotes (RFC 5545: DST gap moves forward, overlap takes the first occurrence) and reports the offset and resolution.
atoms.notes: Python uses the pinned tzdata package only (zoneinfo.reset_tzpath); TypeScript uses Intl (browser IANA data). Vectors are fixed to tzdata 2026.5 rules.

atoms.purpose: Returns the first and last local date an event covers for a viewer in a given zone: all-day events keep their dates, timed events are placed by their UTC instants.
atoms.notes: Used by the day/week/month views (HAAL-060, 087, 088) and for shared calendars across zones.

atoms.purpose: Default (missing = medium), order (high → low with a module tie-break) and filter (set of levels, empty = all) of item priorities; the server uses the same order in SQL.
atoms.notes: SQL helpers rank_sql / filter_sql live next to the Python implementation; UI in frontend/src/components/ui/priority.tsx; bulk set_priority for events, notes and cards in haalendar.bulk (HAAL-041).

flows.purpose: Header shows the Week A/B label of the selected date (FR-CAL-05).
Registration validates the password with the policy atom before hashing (FR-ACC-01).

First-run wizard: while no administrator exists the SPA redirects to /setup; creating the first admin checks the setup token, validates the password with the policy atom (live in the browser, authoritative on the server) and signs in (FR-ACC-05).
Invitation page: the invited address is shown from the token, the password is checked live with the policy atom and again on registration, then the invitee is signed in (FR-ACC-06).
Every content request: session resolved → app.user_id set for the transaction (RLS) → container facts loaded → authz.check decides → 404/403 or the action runs (FR-ACC-07).
Share / change / revoke: the container owner is checked with authz.check (action share) under row-level security; a grantee may only leave; revocation is soft (FR-ACC-10).
Event times: local date/time + tzid are stored; start_utc/end_utc derived with time.local_to_utc; views place events on the viewer's days with time.event_days (FR-ACC-11).
Open sign-up, password reset and password change check the new password live and on the server with the policy atom (FR-ACC-01, FR-ACC-02).
Lists of events, notes and cards sort and filter by priority with the same rules on the server (SQL) and in the web app (local, offline) (FR-X-12).
Settings show this and next week's Week A/B label while the user edits it (FR-CAL-23, D-50).
